Hi Samira — thanks for sending this over. I pulled together answers and an executive summary attached (redwood-answer-summary-2026-07-28.pdf). Key points below; full answers are in the PDF + spreadsheet.

- Data residency: Hosted API requests are processed in the region you select when provisioning (we currently offer eu-west-1, us-west-2, and ap-southeast-1). Request payloads and generated content are stored in encrypted object storage in that region by default. Metadata (request timestamp, model id, token counts) may be replicated to the control plane for billing and routing purposes; replicas are encrypted and limited to metadata only.

- Retention windows: Customer request/response payloads are retained by default for 30 days for quality monitoring and debug (configurable to 0 days on a per-customer basis for customers with contractual requirements). Billing and usage metering data (aggregated) retained for 13 months to support billing reconciliation. Audit logs that contain operational metadata are retained for 1 year; access is limited and logged.

- Deletion / erasure: Customers can request account-level erasure via the console or support ticket. Deletion process: (1) mark the data for purge; (2) remove from primary object storage within 48 hours; (3) remove or rekey any cached keys and KV caches within 72 hours; (4) trigger background purge for backups/replicas (see backups note) — final propagation complete within 30 days. We provide a deletion certificate on completion.

- Backups & replicas: We maintain short-lived snapshots for disaster recovery. Snapshots are encrypted and stored in-region; snapshot retention is 7 days by default. For customers requiring no backups, negotiation of a no-backup contract term is possible for Dedicated/Private deployments — for Hosted API, we can reduce snapshot retention to 0 for certain enterprise contracts.

- Controls: All data at rest is AES-256 encrypted. Keys are managed in a customer-isolated KMS for Dedicated/Private; for Hosted API we use cloud KMS with envelope encryption; customer-managed KMS is available via our Private offering (we noted this as an option in the PDF). We are SOC 2 Type II compliant; encryption-in-transit is TLS1.2+; role-based access controls and IAM audit trails apply.

I've CC'd Irene and Ben for one-line confirmation on audit log retention and billing retention numbers. If that looks good, I can convert the PDF into the Excel template you sent.

Oliver — thanks for the precise questions. Short answers here and we'll push a one-page addendum to the PDF.

1) KV cache persistence: In the Hosted API, model KV caches used during generation are kept in-memory on the inference host for the life of the request and short-lived batching windows. We do not write those in-memory caches to persistent disk under normal operation. In rare manual troubleshooting scenarios we may capture memory dumps under strict access controls and with customer approval; that is documented and requires a support ticket and e-signed consent.

2) Deletion certificate: The certificate includes the account id, scope of data erased (request ids / date ranges), the deletion workflow run id, timestamps for each purge stage, and the operator/service that executed the purge (automated service or specific support team). We typically provide the certificate within 5 business days after final propagation (i.e., after the 30-day backup propagation window), but for standard cases where retention is 30 days and there are no special backup contracts, the whole process completes inside 30 days and the certificate is issued within 5 business days thereafter. If Rosebank requires a faster certificate timeline, we can discuss contractual SLA adjustments.
